text:
maria_support: heads-up — customer ACME reported large spike in tail latency and intermittent 403s starting ~03:20 UTC. They say requests are landing in hosted (us-west2) even though their dedicated pin is eu-west1. ticket: ACME-982
ethan_sre: on it. do we have routing logs or a pin TTL refresh around that time?
maria_support: yes — saw a pin ttl refresh at 03:18 and then mass fallbacks at 03:20. snippet from routing logs:
```
[2026-03-15T03:18:02Z] pin_refresh: customer=acme; pin=eu-west1; ttl=3600
[2026-03-15T03:20:09Z] route_decide: req_id=aa1; customer=acme; desired_pool=dedicated-eu-01; pin_lookup=MISS; fallback=hosted-us-west2
[2026-03-15T03:20:09Z] proxy_upstream: upstream=hosted-us-west2; auth=200; latency_ms=712
[2026-03-15T03:20:10Z] proxy_upstream: upstream=hosted-us-west2; auth=403; latency_ms=905
```
maria_support: customer sees higher token costs and cross-region latency — they're getting billed at hosted rates.
jay_platform: hypothesis: pin refresh logic bumped the pin into a transient state that lost affinity to the dedicated pool, then routing policy allowed cross-region fallbacks. can you repro locally with ttl manipulation?
ethan_sre: repro steps I ran:
1) create a test tenant with dedicated-eu pin
2) set pin.ttl to 1s and refresh
3) flood ~50 concurrent requests with X-Region: eu-west1 header
Result: ~20% routed to hosted-us-west2, auth still passing sometimes but higher 5xx/403 rates
Commands I used:
```bash
for i in {1..60}; do \
  curl -s -H "X-Customer: acme" -H "X-Region: eu-west1" https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate &
done
```
jay_platform: thanks — that matches. logs show pin store returning stale metadata during the refresh window. likely race between pin-ttl refresh and store compaction.
nora_billing: ACME billing alert triggered — +120% hosted usage last hour. are we able to issue credits? need to know exact hosted token counts per hour for the spike window.
alex_prod: short-term mitigation: set routing policy for ACME to `allow_fallback=false` (will surface 503s instead of cross-region hosted fallbacks) and refresh the dedicated pool binding manually. patch I deployed to the control plane to force rebind: `rbacctl rebind --customer acme --pool dedicated-eu-01`
ethan_sre: also adding a quick fix: prevent pin.ttl from being set < 30s during active refresh windows to avoid losing affinity. longer-term: fix store compaction race and add metric for "pin-lookup-miss-during-refresh"
ops-bot: created incident INC-2026-234 and paging oncall SRE.
support-bot: noted on ticket ACME-982 — added logs and recommended workaround steps.
maria_support: customer accepted temporary credits if we confirm hosted token delta and ETA for permanent fix. I'll own customer comms. please update ACME-982 with numbers and expected timeline. :pray:
ethan_sre: collecting per-customer hosted token counts now, will post in thread when I have the numbers.
jay_platform: filing a follow-up engineering task: ENG-1278 "pin store compaction race causing hosted fallback"
alex_prod: if anybody needs the quick rollback I can revert the routing policy change after we validate. :thumbsup:
